Name: Cities of London and Westminster
Description: A central London constituency combining the financial district of the City of London with Westminster's political and commercial heart. It includes some of Britain's wealthiest residential areas, such as Mayfair and Belgravia, alongside younger, more transient and rented communities around areas such as Soho, Covent Garden and parts of Pimlico.

Name: Kensington and Bayswater
Description: A highly diverse and socially polarised constituency spanning parts of Kensington and Chelsea and Westminster. South Kensington is among London's wealthiest areas, while North Kensington contains more diverse and lower-income communities, including the historic Afro-Caribbean community around Notting Hill and the area associated with the Notting Hill Carnival. Bayswater adds a more mixed central London character, with a large private-rented population and significant international community.

Name: Chelsea and Fulham
County: London (Hammersmith and Fulham; Kensington and Chelsea)
Description: One of London's most affluent constituencies, covering wealthy areas along the Thames including Chelsea and Fulham. It contains some of the highest property prices in the country, although Fulham has a large private-rented population and a younger, more transient professional population.

Name: Hampstead and Highgate
Description: An affluent and highly educated North London constituency centred around Hampstead and Highgate. Hampstead is known for high property prices, celebrity residents, literary associations and prestigious private schools, giving it one of the highest rates of private school attendance in the country. Despite its wealth, the area has traditionally had a strong progressive and liberal political culture, often described as 'Hampstead liberalism'.

Name: Finchley and Golders Green
Description: Finchley and Golders Green is an affluent and highly educated north London constituency with a large professional population. It is particularly notable for its sizeable Jewish community, especially around Golders Green, where Jewish residents form a majority, making it one of the largest Jewish communities in Europe. Increasing diversity, a growing South Asian population, younger residents and a rise in private renting - particularly in the Finchley half of the seat - have made the seat more politically competitive in recent years.

Name: Richmond Park
County: London (Kingston upon Thames; Richmond upon Thames)
Description: Covering Richmond Park, Barnes and North Kingston, this is one of Britain's most affluent and highly educated constituencies. Professional occupations, graduate qualifications and owner occupation are among the highest in Britain. The seat voted overwhelmingly against Brexit in the 2016 referendum.

Name: Wimbledon
Description: An affluent suburban constituency in south-west London, known internationally for Wimbledon tennis and characterised by high levels of professional employment, owner occupation and educational attainment. It contains both wealthy residential areas, particularly Wimbledon Village, and more mixed communities around parts of Wimbledon town.

Name: Hammersmith and Chiswick
Description: Stretching from urban, primarily renting and gentrifying Hammersmith to the leafy suburbs of Chiswick, this constituency combines two distinct west London identities. Chiswick is affluent, highly educated and popular with professionals, while Hammersmith is denser, younger and has much higher levels of private renting. Excellent transport links and proximity to central London make it attractive to commuters.

Name: Battersea
Description: Once a heavily industrial and working-class constituency centred on the Thames, Battersea has undergone extensive gentrification since the 1980s. Today it is characterised by young graduates, highly educated professionals and City workers, particularly around Clapham Junction, Nine Elms and the Battersea Power Station redevelopment, although pockets of social housing remain.

Name: Ealing Central and Acton
Description: Stretching from leafy Ealing Broadway to the busy urban districts of Acton, this is a socially mixed west London constituency. Regeneration and excellent transport links have attracted growing numbers of young professionals, while long-established Irish, Polish and Asian communities remain important parts of the area's identity. Housing ranges from affluent Victorian suburbs in the 'Ealing Central' part of the constituency to modern apartment developments.

Name: Runnymede and Weybridge
Description: A Surrey seat combining Chertsey and Egham with the wealthy town of Weybridge, home to exclusive private estates and the Wentworth golf course. It also includes Runnymede meadow, site of the Magna Carta, and Royal Holloway University, alongside more mixed, ex-council housing around Addlestone.

Name: Esher and Walton
Description: Part of Surrey's 'stockbroker belt', combining the exclusive gated estates around Esher and Sandown Park racecourse with the more mixed, ordinary suburbs of Walton, Molesey and Hersham. It is exceptionally affluent and highly qualified overall, though with pockets of social housing.

Name: Putney
Description: A prosperous south-west London constituency combining riverside Putney with more suburban Roehampton and Southfields. It has a highly educated population, very high levels of professional and managerial employment, and large numbers of graduates and young professionals. While affluent overall, Roehampton contains some of London's largest post-war housing estates, making the constituency socially mixed.

Name: Brentford and Isleworth
Description: A socially mixed west London constituency stretching from the regenerated riverside at Brentford to the suburban communities of Isleworth and Osterley. The area combines young professionals attracted by redevelopment with long-established suburban neighbourhoods. Heathrow and major employers along the M4 corridor have also shaped the local economy. The constituency has a large Asian community.

Name: Poplar and Limehouse
Description: Poplar and Limehouse combines some of Britain's most deprived neighbourhoods with the skyscrapers and financial district of Canary Wharf. Large Bangladeshi, Muslim and other ethnic minority communities sit alongside growing numbers of highly paid professionals living in new riverside developments, creating high rates of both social and private renting.

Name: Clapham and Brixton Hill
Description: A young, highly educated, dense inner London constituency combining socially mixed Clapham with the diverse communities of Brixton Hill. Extensive gentrification has brought growing numbers of graduates and professionals, while the area retains a significant Black population and vibrant cultural scene. Private and social renting, graduate population and professional employment are amongst the highest in the country.

Name: Dulwich and West Norwood
Description: A socially diverse inner London constituency combining affluent Dulwich with the more mixed communities of West Norwood, Herne Hill and Tulse Hill. Dulwich is known for its historic village atmosphere, large Victorian homes and prestigious schools, while parts of Lambeth have significant Afro-Caribbean and African communities.

Name: Islington South and Finsbury
Description: Stretching from Clerkenwell and Farringdon to Canonbury and Highbury, this constituency covers some of London's most densely populated neighbourhoods. It is a socially polarised seat of affluent graduates, professionals and gentrified neighbourhoods such as Angel, alongside private renters and significant social housing. Major cultural, educational and technology institutions contribute to its cosmopolitan and highly international character.

Name: Beaconsfield
Description: An affluent Buckinghamshire commuter seat of small towns and villages between the M40 and M25, including Marlow on the Thames and the exceptionally wealthy Gerrards Cross. Overwhelmingly owner-occupied and professional, with only small pockets of less prosperous housing.

Name: Bethnal Green and Stepney
Description: An ethnically diverse constituency, with large Bangladeshi, Bengali and Muslim communities alongside growing young professional populations. Historically a working-class East End seat, it combines high levels of social deprivation with rapid regeneration and gentrification. Private and social renting are both exceptionally common.

Name: Cambridge
Description: The University of Cambridge, technology and life sciences industries, and the wider "Silicon Fen" economy give the city a highly skilled and internationally diverse population, whilst Cambridge also has a very large student and private renting population

Name: Chesham and Amersham
Description: A wealthy Chiltern Hills seat combining the commuter town of Chesham, with pockets of more modest housing, and the increasingly affluent Amersham and Chalfonts to the south. Highly owner-occupied and professional, it is one of the most prosperous corners of Buckinghamshire.

Name: Chipping Barnet
Description: A prosperous suburban constituency characterised by detached housing, high owner occupation, its Jewish community, and an older population. While traditionally Conservative, increasing ethnic diversity and an influx of younger professionals have made the seat more politically competitive. It remains one of London's archetypal middle-class suburbs.

Name: Enfield North
Description: Enfield North combines established suburban neighbourhoods with more diverse urban communities around Ponders End. Once a predominantly white commuter area, it has become increasingly multicultural, including a significant Turkish and Cypriot community.

Name: Guildford
Description: Surrey's county town, combining a wealthy commuter core and the University of Surrey with more working-class estates such as Park Barn and Bellfields. It has a large student population and a strong tradition of local environmental and anti-development activism.

Name: Harpenden and Berkhamsted
Description: A highly affluent and well educated constituency centered on prospeours Hertfordshire commuter towns. High property prices, professional employment and exceptionally high levels of degree attainment give the area a strongly middle-class character, with many residents commuting into London or working in professional and knowledge-based industries

Name: Harrow East
Description: An affluent and suburban constituency on London's north-western edge. It has one of Britain's largest Hindu and Indian populations, alongside a sizeable Muslim and Romanian population and a Jewish community in Stanmore, making it one of London's most religiously diverse suburban seats. Residential neighbourhoods dominate, with relatively little social housing by London standards.

Name: Harrow West
Description: Harrow West is a diverse suburban constituency with substantial Indian, Gujarati and Hindu populations, as well as growing Black and Muslim communities. Compared with Harrow East, it has a younger population, higher levels of private renting and greater social diversity. The area combines established suburban housing with denser urban neighbourhoods around Harrow town centre.

Name: Hendon
Description: A socially mixed north London constituency combining affluent suburban neighbourhoods with large post-war housing estates and new high-rise development and a growing number of private renters. It has sizeable Jewish, Muslim and increasingly diverse ethnic minority communities, alongside a highly educated professional population. A very polarised constituency between more Jewish, suburban and middle-class areas like Edgware, and more working-class, multi-ethnic communities in places like Cricklewood.

Name: Hornsey and Friern Barnet
Description: This intellectual north London constituency combines the affluent, progressive neighbourhoods of Crouch End, Muswell Hill and Friern Barnet. It has a highly educated population, large numbers of graduates and professionals, and a substantial private-rented sector. Green spaces such as Alexandra Park and Highgate Wood are a defining feature of the area.

Name: Islington North
Description: Jeremy Corbyn's longtime constituency, Islington North combines affluent gentrified neighbourhoods with extensive social housing. It has a young, highly educated population alongside long-established working-class communities. High levels of private and social renting, public sector employment and political activism are defining features of the constituency. It is also the densest and geographically smallest constituency in Britain.

Name: Maidenhead
Description: An affluent Berkshire town on the Thames, taking in the villages of Cookham and Bray. Overwhelmingly professional and owner-occupied, it ranks among the wealthiest constituencies in the country.

Name: Mid Buckinghamshire
Description: An unusually rural Buckinghamshire seat with no large towns, spanning the Vale of Aylesbury's farmland and the plush villages of the Chiltern Hills, and home to Chequers, the Prime Minister's country residence. It has a prosperous, largely middle-class and settled character.

Name: Oxford West and Abingdon
Description: Combining north Oxford's university suburbs, home to every Oxford college, with the historic market town of Abingdon to the south. Highly educated and professional, it has a large student population and strong links to nearby science research sites.

Name: Ruislip, Northwood and Pinner
Description: One of London's most affluent suburban constituencies, characterised by detached housing, leafy streets and high levels of owner occupation. Northwood and Pinner are particularly prosperous, while Ruislip combines suburban neighbourhoods with extensive green space. The constituency has a large professional and managerial workforce. Unlike the suburban parts of Bromley, it is a highly ethnically diverse seat, with a large Hindu population.

Name: South West Hertfordshire
Description: An affluent Hertfordshire commuter seat centred on Rickmansworth and the wealthy villages of Chorleywood and Croxley Green, alongside the very different council estate of South Oxhey. It has a highly professional population and a substantial and growing Indian and Hindu community.

Name: Southgate and Wood Green
Description: This constituency combines the affluent suburbs of Southgate with the denser and more diverse communities of Wood Green. Southgate retains much of its inter-war suburban character, while Wood Green has experienced rapid demographic change and regeneration. The constituency has one of the largest proportions of non-British white residents owing to its large Greek, Turkish and Cypriot communities, as well as more recent immigrants from Eastern Europe.

Name: Streatham and Croydon North
Description: Spanning parts of Lambeth and Croydon, this constituency combines Streatham's increasingly affluent neighbourhoods with the diverse communities of north Croydon. Both areas have experienced significant demographic change, driven by a growing Black middle class, younger professionals and public sector employment. Streatham High Road is one of Europe's longest continuous shopping streets.

Name: Tooting
Description: A young, diverse and highly educated inner London constituency with large numbers of private renters, graduates and professional workers. Tooting has long been known for its large South Asian community - particularly around Tooting Broadway - as well as its internationally renowned food scene. The presence of St George's Hospital makes healthcare one of the area's largest employers.

Name: Twickenham
Description: An affluent, highly educated and socially liberal suburban constituency in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames. It has one of the highest proportions of professional and managerial occupations in the country, alongside high levels of owner occupation and graduate qualifications.

Name: Windsor
Description: Home to Windsor Castle and Eton College, this Berkshire seat also takes in the racecourse town of Ascot and exclusive estates such as Virginia Water. It is socially varied, ranging from very wealthy areas to more ordinary social housing near Slough.

Name: Woking
Description: A cosmopolitan Surrey town with a large Asian population and a significant Muslim community centred on one of England's oldest mosques. It combines wealthy villages such as Pyrford with high-rise estates like Sheerwater, and was the setting for the Martian invasion in H.G. Wells's War of the Worlds.

Name: Hackney South and Shoreditch
Description: Covering Shoreditch, Hoxton and southern Hackney, this constituency has become synonymous with London's creative and technology sectors. Rapid gentrification has attracted young graduates and professionals, although significant deprivation and social housing remain. It is among the youngest and most ethnically diverse constituencies in Britain, with a significant Black population. Socially it is very mixed, with long-standing working-class council estates existing alongside leafy, gentrified Victorian neighbourhoods.

Name: Vauxhall and Camberwell Green
Description: The constituency is an inner-London seat covering Waterloo, Kennington, South Lambeth, Stockwell and parts of Camberwell, combining affluent riverside developments with large council estates. It is highly diverse, with large Black Caribbean and Black African communities, a notable Portuguese population, and a socially liberal professional electorate alongside a significant working-class population. Levels of both private and social renting are high, and there is a significant LGBTQ+ community centred around Vauxhall. Major redevelopment continues to transform Nine Elms and the surrounding area.

Name: Aberdeen South
Description: Southern Aberdeen, from affluent western suburbs like Cults and Milltimber to more industrial and coastal areas in the east. The local economy is closely tied to North Sea oil and gas, and Aberdeen Airport doubles as one of the world's busiest heliports for rig workers. A socially mixed seat, with some of Scotland's wealthiest and most deprived areas close together.

Name: Altrincham and Sale West
Description: An affluent, leafy Trafford commuter suburb southwest of Manchester, taking in Altrincham, Sale, Hale and Bowdon. It has one of the highest concentrations of managerial and professional workers in the North West, a large industrial and retail park at Broadheath, and a notable Jewish community.

Name: Arundel and South Downs
Description: A large, affluent West Sussex seat covering much of the South Downs, centred on the small towns of Arundel, with its historic castle, and Petworth. Overwhelmingly white and owner-occupied, it draws heavily on tourism and country-estate heritage.

Name: Bermondsey and Old Southwark
Description: A central London constituency combining the historic riverside districts of Bermondsey and Southwark. Once heavily industrial and working class, much of the area has experienced rapid gentrification, attracting young professionals while retaining significant social housing. The constituency is socially diverse and politically progressive.

Name: Bromley and Biggin Hill
Description: A predominantly affluent suburban constituency in the south of the London Borough of Bromley. It combines the prosperous suburban town of Bromley with the more semi-rural community of Biggin Hill on the edge of Greater London. The seat has high levels of owner occupation and relatively little social housing compared with most London constituencies.

Name: Croydon East
Description: An ethnically diverse, suburban constituency covering the eastern side of Croydon, characterised by high levels of home ownership, a large Black community and relatively affluent neighbourhoods. It combines established commuter suburbs with more mixed areas around Addiscombe and Shirley.

Name: Croydon South
Description: One of London's most affluent suburban constituencies, stretching from Purley to Coulsdon and the edge of the North Downs. It has very high levels of owner occupation, low levels of social housing and an older, predominantly middle-class population. The constituency has long been a Conservative stronghold.

Name: Dorking and Horley
Description: A Surrey Hills constituency taking in the market town of Dorking, beneath Box Hill and Leith Hill, and the more workaday town of Horley near Gatwick Airport. Affluent and elderly overall, it also has a noted brewing and vineyard heritage around Dorking.

Name: Earley and Woodley
Description: A modern, planned suburban seat east of Reading, combining Earley and Woodley, neither of which existed as significant towns before the twentieth century. Home to part of Reading University's campus, it has a notably diverse population for Berkshire.

Name: Epsom and Ewell
Description: An affluent Surrey commuter seat built around Epsom, Ewell and its famous racecourse, extending to Ashtead and Leatherhead. Wealthy and heavily owner-occupied, it has an unusually strong tradition of independent 'Residents Association' politics rather than party loyalty.

Name: Farnham and Bordon
Description: A cross-border Surrey and Hampshire seat combining the historic market town of Farnham, with its Norman castle, and the hillside town of Haslemere with the much less affluent former garrison town of Bordon, redeveloped since its army camp closed. The Surrey towns are noticeably wealthier than the Hampshire side.

Name: Godalming and Ash
Description: A wealthy, rural Surrey seat centred on Godalming and Cranleigh, home to the private schools Charterhouse and Cranleigh School. Mostly affluent and owner-occupied, with a scattering of picture-postcard villages, though the Ash salient to the north has a more working-class, Camberley-facing character.

Name: Greenwich and Woolwich
Description: A diverse, historically industrial constituency on the south bank of the Thames, undergoing rapid regeneration through major housing developments. It has significant Black and Asian communities, high levels of both social and private renting, and one of the youngest populations in the country, with relatively few pensioners.

Name: Henley and Thame
Description: An affluent Oxfordshire seat combining the rowing town of Henley-on-Thames with Thame and the Chiltern Hills, and villages used as filming locations for Midsomer Murders. Overwhelmingly professional and owner-occupied, it is solidly upper-middle-class commuter territory.

Name: Hertsmere
Description: A distinctive and diverse Hertfordshire constituency combining the London adjacent towns of Borehamwood, Bushey, Potters Bar and Radlett. It has a particularly large Jewish population, especially in parts of Bushey and Radlett, alongside significant Indian and other minority communities. The constituency combines affluent commuter suburbs with more mixed urban areas, while Borehamwood is also known for its major film and television industry.

Name: Holborn and St Pancras
Description: Covering much of central Camden, this constituency combines historic Bloomsbury, King's Cross and Holborn with the fashionable neighbourhoods of Kentish Town and Camden Town. It has exceptionally high levels of private and social renting, students, graduates and professional employment, alongside significant social housing. Major institutions including the British Museum, UCL and LSE (including most of their student accommodation) and the legal quarter give the constituency an unusually international character. A fifth of residents are Muslim, owing to the significant Bangladeshi community in Somers Town.

Name: Kingston and Surbiton
Description: Kingston and Surbiton is an affluent suburban constituency with high levels of graduate qualifications and professional employment. Kingston's university gives the area a sizeable student and private-renting population, while Surbiton is known for its leafy residential streets and commuter character. The south of the constituency around Chessington has more White lower-middle-class residents, and New Malden is known for its Korean community.

Name: Lewisham West and East Dulwich
Description: A socially mixed inner south London constituency combining the affluent and increasingly expensive neighbourhoods of East Dulwich with the more diverse communities of northern Lewisham. The seat has experienced significant gentrification, while retaining a large Black community, high levels of public sector employment and a strong creative and cultural presence.

Name: Milton Keynes North
Description: The northern part of Milton Keynes, taking in the historic railway town of Wolverton and market town of Stony Stratford, along with newer suburban estates and rural villages further north. It has a wide social mix, from affluent villages to more working-class newer developments.

Name: Newbury
Description: A West Berkshire seat centred on Newbury, with the racehorse-training village of Lambourn and the former Greenham Common airbase nearby. Affluent, rural and overwhelmingly professional, it is classic Home Counties commuter territory.

Name: Old Bexley and Sidcup
Description: A suburban outer London constituency centred on the historic towns of Old Bexley and Sidcup, both of which retain strong Kentish identities. The seat is characterised by high levels of owner occupation, relatively little private or social renting, and a predominantly lower middle-class population, with many residents employed in professional, administrative and public sector occupations.

Name: Orpington
Description: A predominantly suburban constituency on London's south-eastern fringe, with exceptionally high levels of owner occupation and among the lowest rates of private and social renting in the capital. Demographically it is one of London's least ethnically diverse and most typically suburban constituencies.

Name: Queen's Park and Maida Vale
Description: This constituency brings together affluent Little Venice, socially mixed Maida Vale, and the more diverse communities of Queen's Park, Kilburn and Kensal Green, known for their Irish community, as well as an Arab community in Lisson Grove. Elegant Victorian terraces sit alongside large council estates, creating one of west London's most socially varied constituencies. High levels of private renting and a young professional population reflect its proximity to central London, while rates of social renting are among the highest, and owner occupation among the lowest, in the country.

Name: Reigate
Description: An affluent commuter seat in eastern Surrey near the M25, centred on Reigate and Redhill beneath the North Downs. It has a strongly professional, owner-occupying population and some of the priciest housing in the region.

Name: Sevenoaks
Description: An affluent West Kent commuter town close to the Surrey border, and home to Winston Churchill's former estate at Chartwell. Swanley, in the north of the seat, is markedly more working-class than wealthy Sevenoaks itself.

Name: South Cambridgeshire
Description: A prosperous ring of villages and small towns encircling Cambridge, from Grantchester to the new town of Cambourne. Many residents work in the university, its research institutes or the wider 'Silicon Fen' economy, giving the seat one of the best-qualified and most professional populations in the country.

Name: Spelthorne
Description: A Surrey seat wedged against Heathrow Airport, taking in Staines, Ashford and Sunbury. Airport-related employment shapes the local economy, and it is noticeably more ethnically diverse near the airport than in its more affluent riverside towns.

Name: St Albans
Description: An affluent cathedral city and commuter town with a historic Roman and medieval centre (reputedly Britain's oldest site of Christian worship) and fast rail links into London. It has one of the highest concentrations of graduates and managerial/professional workers in the country, alongside a small but notable Bangladeshi community.

Name: Stratford and Bow
Description: Centred on Stratford, Bow and the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, this constituency has undergone some of London's most dramatic regeneration since the 2012 Olympics. It has a young, ethnically diverse population (around a third of whom are Muslim) and high levels of both private and social renting. New high-rise developments stand alongside long-established East End communities.

Name: Sutton and Cheam
Description: A suburban outer London seat in the London Borough of Sutton, historically one of London's more traditional and less diverse commuter areas. It has a growing and increasingly significant Hindu and Indian community, alongside a notable Chinese population, giving it a more diverse profile than its reputation might suggest.

Name: Tatton
Description: One of the most affluent seats outside London, taking in the wealthy commuter towns of Wilmslow, Alderley Edge and Knutsford near Manchester Airport. Home to major pharmaceutical, finance and insurance employers, with the historic Tatton Park estate as its centrepiece.

Name: Wokingham
Description: An affluent stockbroker-belt seat of villages and small towns east of Reading, including Finchampstead, Twyford and Wargrave. Overwhelmingly owner-occupied and highly professional, it is one of the least deprived constituencies in the country.

Name: Hackney North and Stoke Newington
Description: Hackney North and Stoke Newington is one of London's most politically progressive constituencies. Once associated with deprivation and council housing, the area has experienced extensive gentrification while retaining large Black, Kurdish and Turkish communities. Young professionals, creatives and long-established residents now live alongside one another. The seat has very high levels of social and private renting, and the north of the constituency is home to a significant Haredi Jewish community.

Name: Aberdeen North
Description: Covers the northern half of Aberdeen, from the university area of Old Aberdeen to the airport and Bridge of Don. Heavily tied to the oil industry, with a large student and rented population, and significant contrasts in deprivation across its wards.

Name: Aldershot
Description: The 'home of the British Army', combining the garrison town of Aldershot with Farnborough, long associated with aviation and its famous airshow. A significant Gurkha and Nepalese community reflects the military connection, and the seat has a notably large Buddhist population for England.

Name: Aylesbury
Description: Buckinghamshire's rapidly expanded county town, historically known for breeding the Aylesbury duck, combining affluent areas such as Bedgrove with more run-down council estates like Southcourt. Surrounding villages in the Vale of Aylesbury add a more rural, traditional character.

Name: Banbury
Description: An Oxfordshire town in the upper Cherwell valley, with a modern industrial base, surrounded by Cotswold villages such as Chipping Norton. It has a notable South Asian community in the Grimsbury area.

Name: Basingstoke
Description: A former market town transformed from the 1960s into a major London-overspill expansion town, with a sprawling, modern core. It has a working population with strong employment rates and a fairly average demographic profile for the South East.

Name: Bath
Description: A UNESCO World Heritage spa city known for its Georgian architecture and Roman baths, home to two universities and a correspondingly large student population. An affluent, highly educated seat reliant on tourism, retail and public services.

Name: Beckenham and Penge
Description: A mainly suburban constituency in western Bromley, combining established middle-class areas such as Beckenham with the more urban and historically working-class area of Penge. The area has experienced significant demographic change in recent decades, becoming more diverse and increasingly connected to inner London.

Name: Bicester and Woodstock
Description: A fast-growing Oxfordshire seat combining the expanding town of Bicester, known for its designer shopping outlet, with the small town of Woodstock, home to Blenheim Palace, and the commuter village of Kidlington. Affluent and largely owner-occupied.

Name: Birmingham Edgbaston
Description: A leafy, middle-class South Birmingham seat centred on the university and cricket ground, taking in the wealthy suburb of Harborne and the more mixed Quinton, alongside the council estates of Bartley Green. It's notably diverse and highly educated, with substantial South Asian and Black communities.

Name: Birmingham Ladywood
Description: Birmingham's city-centre seat, taking in the Jewellery Quarter and a mix of regenerated canalside development with deprived inner areas such as Winson Green. It has a young, highly diverse population with a large Muslim majority and some of the highest social housing rates outside London.

Name: Bracknell
Description: A post-war new town amid Berkshire pine forests, now home to major technology firms along the M4 corridor. It also includes Sandhurst, home of the Royal Military Academy, and the prestigious Wellington College.

Name: Brent East
Description: A highly diverse suburban constituency with one of the largest Black and Asian populations in the UK. Housing ranges from inter-war suburbs to dense urban neighbourhoods with high levels of private and social renting. Labour's support reflects the constituency's young, multicultural and metropolitan character.

Name: Brent West
Description: A densely populated and highly diverse constituency covering parts of Willesden and Harlesden. Demographically it is majority Asian, with a significant Hindu Indian population, high levels of private renting and a comparatively young population, with significant regeneration around Wembley Stadium.

Name: Brentwood and Ongar
Description: A prosperous constituency combining the affluent London commuter town of Brentwood with the smaller market town of Ongar and the surrounding rural Essex countryside.

Name: Brighton Kemptown and Peacehaven
Description: Combining Brighton's Kemptown, known for its LGBT community and student population, with the council estates of Moulsecoomb and Whitehawk and the more affluent coastal towns of Rottingdean, Saltdean and Peacehaven further east. A socially varied seat along the Sussex coast.

Name: Brighton Pavilion
Description: Central Brighton, taking in the Royal Pavilion, seafront and the Lanes shopping district, alongside the University of Sussex campus. Known for its large LGBT community and student population, it has an unusually young, highly educated and diverse profile, often described as 'London by the sea'.

Name: Bristol Central
Description: Bristol's wealthy, liberal core, covering Clifton, Redland and Montpellier along with the university and city centre. An exceptionally young, highly educated and heavily private-renting seat, with a large student population.

Name: Bristol North West
Description: Runs from the wealthy Downs and Stoke Bishop in the south to Avonmouth's docks and the working-class Lawrence Weston estate in the north. A mixed seat combining large houses, inter-war council estates and light industry.

Name: Buckingham and Bletchley
Description: Combining the historic market town of Buckingham with Bletchley, part of Milton Keynes and once the wartime home of the codebreakers at Bletchley Park. It bridges a modern, ethnically mixed New Town population with more traditional rural Buckinghamshire.

Name: Carshalton and Wallington
Description: A suburban outer London constituency in Sutton, characterised by leafy residential areas, high home ownership and relatively affluent households. Compared with neighbouring Lib Dem-friendly south-west London seats, it has a more traditional suburban character and voted to leave the EU in 2016.

Name: Cheadle
Description: An affluent Stockport commuter suburb of Greater Manchester, including Bramhall, Cheadle Hulme and Heald Green, with one of the highest owner-occupation rates in the country. It has a notably large Jewish community and low levels of social housing.

Name: Cheltenham
Description: A Regency spa town known for horse racing and its literature festival, combining wealthy Georgian suburbs such as Montpellier with council estates like Hester's Way. A well-educated, professional seat with sharp internal contrasts in affluence.

Name: Chester South and Eddisbury
Description: A rural southwest Cheshire seat of villages and small market towns such as Tarporley and Malpas, plus the salt-mining town of Winsford, historically Liverpool overspill and demographically distinct from the surrounding countryside. High owner-occupation and low social housing overall.

Name: Chichester
Description: A cathedral city in West Sussex, with the Goodwood estate, home to horse and motor racing, and the seaside town of Selsey nearby. Affluent and elderly, it draws on tourism, racing and a significant public-sector presence.

Name: Chingford and Woodford Green
Description: A leafy outer London constituency with high levels of home ownership and relatively low deprivation. Traditionally one of London's more Conservative suburbs, it combines affluent Woodford Green with the more socially mixed communities of Chingford. Residents are generally older and less ethnically diverse than London as a whole.

Name: Chippenham
Description: A west Wiltshire commuter seat centred on the market town of Chippenham, with the historic wool town of Calne and the military-linked town of Corsham nearby. A fairly typical, middle-class constituency within easy reach of Bath, Bristol and Swindon.

Name: Coventry South
Description: Coventry's most middle-class seat, combining the city centre and university with affluent southern suburbs such as Earlsdon and Finham. It has an above-average graduate rate and a notable Sikh community.

Name: Crawley
Description: A post-war new town built around Gatwick Airport, a major local employer. More ethnically diverse and higher-renting than the rest of West Sussex, with a mix of council-built estates and newer private housing.

Name: Didcot and Wantage
Description: A mixed Oxfordshire seat combining the railway town of Didcot, a former coal power station site, with the historic market town of Wantage, birthplace of King Alfred the Great. It is also home to major scientific research centres at Harwell and Culham.

Name: Ealing North
Description: Ealing North is a diverse suburban constituency with large Indian, Somali and Polish communities. It combines established residential suburbs with denser neighbourhoods around Greenford and Perivale, and has a relatively balanced mix of owner occupation, private renting and social housing.

Name: Ealing Southall
Description: Known for its renowned Sikh and Punjabi community, Ealing Southall is one of Britain's most culturally distinctive constituencies. Southall has long been a centre of South Asian life, with vibrant shopping streets, temples and restaurants. The constituency is densely populated and ethnically diverse.

Name: East Grinstead and Uckfield
Description: An affluent, wooded West Sussex seat centred on the towns of East Grinstead and Uckfield, with private schools such as Ardingly nearby. East Grinstead is also home to the UK headquarters of the Church of Scientology.

Name: East Ham
Description: East Ham is one of the country's most ethnically diverse constituencies, with one of the lowest White populations of any UK seat and a majority-Asian population. Historically a working-class East London suburb, it now has high levels of private renting, relatively little owner occupation and a young population. Immigration has played a major role in shaping the area's modern identity.

Name: East Hampshire
Description: A prosperous, rural Hampshire seat centred on the market towns of Alton and Petersfield, with literary connections to Jane Austen at Chawton and naturalist Gilbert White at Selborne. Affluent and owner-occupied, it has a quiet, largely off-the-beaten-track character.

Name: East Surrey
Description: A leafy, affluent Surrey seat along the North Downs, centred on Caterham and Oxted with the village of Lingfield and its racecourse. Highly owner-occupied and car-dependent, with only small pockets of social housing.

Name: East Wiltshire
Description: A long, rural strip of Wiltshire running from the edge of Swindon down through the Vale of Pewsey to the Salisbury Avon valley, dominated by Salisbury Plain's army ranges. It also includes Stonehenge and the ancient monument at Avebury.

Name: Edinburgh East and Musselburgh
Description: Runs from Edinburgh's historic Old Town, centred on tourism around the Royal Mile, to the coastal towns of Portobello and Musselburgh. Some outlying estates such as Craigmillar and Niddrie remain among the city's more deprived areas, contrasting with increasingly gentrified Portobello.

Name: Edinburgh North and Leith
Description: Northern Edinburgh, running from the elegant New Town down to the port of Leith and the Firth of Forth. Leith has been extensively regenerated and gentrified in recent decades, though some council estates like Granton and Pilton remain deprived.

Name: Edinburgh South
Description: Combines affluent Morningside and Marchmont with suburban areas and ex-council estates further south. A large student population clusters around the University of Edinburgh, and the EH10 postcode is reputedly Scotland's most expensive.

Name: Edinburgh South West
Description: Spans from the city centre to affluent southern suburbs like Colinton and Currie, and separately takes in working-class areas including Wester Hailes and Sighthill. Redford Barracks, home to Scottish army regiments, sits on the more affluent Pentland Hills fringe. A socially varied seat with a strong professional presence.

Name: Edinburgh West
Description: Covers northwest Edinburgh, from upmarket Dean Village and Murrayfield through suburban Blackhall and Davidson's Mains to South Queensferry and the Forth bridges. An affluent, highly educated and professional seat, with Edinburgh Airport nearby.

Name: Edmonton and Winchmore Hill
Description: This constituency brings together the affluent suburb of Winchmore Hill with the more diverse and deprived communities of Edmonton. The contrast between the two areas creates one of north London's most socially varied constituencies.

Name: Eltham and Chislehurst
Description: A suburban constituency combining the socially mixed communities of Eltham with the more affluent and traditionally suburban areas of Chislehurst. Eltham has historic links to the Royal Arsenal and a more diverse population, while Chislehurst reflects the more affluent character of neighbouring Bromley.

Name: Ely and East Cambridgeshire
Description: Rural constituency that contains historic Ely, market towns such as Sonham, and numerous agricultural villages. Many residents commute into Cambridge and its science parks. The constituency combines productive farmland with a relatively affluent and professional population.

Name: Epping Forest
Description: A diverse and affluent commuter-belt constituency. It combines suburban towns such as Loughton, Chigwell and Waltham Abbey with more rural communities around Epping and Theydon Bois. Strong transport links and proximity to London have created a wealthy, professional population, while the constituency also contains significant Jewish and South Asian communities.

Name: Feltham and Heston
Description: Located on London's western edge, this constituency combines suburban neighbourhoods with areas shaped by Heathrow Airport and its related industries. Large South Asian communities, particularly around Heston, including both Sikhs and Hindus, contribute to its diverse character. The population is relatively young, with a growing private rental sector.

Name: Glasgow North
Description: Glasgow's West End university quarter and city centre, plus more industrial northern neighbourhoods like Maryhill along the Forth and Clyde Canal. A young, highly studentified seat with a mix of gentrified tenements and areas of high deprivation.

Name: Gordon and Buchan
Description: Rural Aberdeenshire towns including Inverurie, Huntly and Ellon, on the northern fringe of Aberdeen. Prosperous and heavily dependent on the fortunes of the North Sea oil industry, with agriculture and whisky distilling also significant.

Name: Harborough, Oadby and Wigston
Description: A diverse constituency combining rural south-east Leicestershire with the suburban towns of Oadby and Wigston, along with the affluent historic town of Market Harborough. Oadby has one of the highest British Indian populations outside Leicester and is mostly middle class, whereas Wigston is more working class

Name: Hayes and Harlington
Description: Centred on Heathrow's eastern edge and containing Heathrow airport, this constituency has long been shaped by aviation, logistics and manufacturing. It has large South Asian communities, particularly of Indian and Punjabi heritage, as well as a large number of Sikhs and Muslims, alongside a growing Somali population. Working-class traditions remain strong, although major regeneration has transformed parts of Hayes in recent years.

Name: Hertford and Stortford
Description: A prosperous constituency that contains the county town of Hertford with its large public sector and the market town of Bishop's Stortford. Strong rail links to London and Cambridge support very high levels of professional employment and graduates

Name: Hitchin
Description: Combining the affluent market town of Hitchin with surrounding rural Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire villages, this is a relatively affluent and highly educated constituency with a strong professional and commuter character.

Name: Hornchurch and Upminster
Description: One of London's most suburban constituencies, Hornchurch and Upminster has high levels of owner occupation, relatively little social housing and an older-than-average population. The area retains strong Essex influences and is characterised by low-density housing, parks and commuter neighbourhoods. Ethnic diversity remains below the London average.

Name: Horsham
Description: A prosperous, fast-growing West Sussex town, surrounded by forest and private schools including Christ's Hospital. Highly owner-occupied and professional, with the RSPCA's national headquarters based nearby in Southwater.

Name: Hove and Portslade
Description: The western part of Brighton and Hove, combining the more sedate residential character of Hove with the industrial, working-class area of Portslade near Shoreham harbour. Once a Conservative stronghold, it has become notably younger and more professional.

Name: Ilford North
Description: A socially mixed suburban constituency combining Redbridge's traditional commuter suburbs with increasingly diverse neighbourhoods. It has a large South Asian and Muslim population alongside established Jewish areas. Home ownership remains relatively high despite growing private renting.

Name: Ilford South
Description: An ethnically diverse, majority Asian constituency, with a particularly large Muslim community. Dense housing, high levels of private renting and relatively low owner occupation give the area a distinctly urban character. The constituency has one of the youngest populations in outer London.

Name: Ipswich
Description: An urban constituency Suffolk's county town and major port. Ipswich combines historic neighbourhoods with more deprived inner-city communities and expanding suburban areas. Its economy is based on the port, public services, and services, while the city has a more ethnically diverse and renter heavy than much of surrounding rural Suffolk.

Name: Kenilworth and Southam
Description: An affluent Warwickshire seat wrapped around Leamington and Warwick, centred on the commuter town of Kenilworth and its ruined castle, with smaller towns such as Southam. It has high rates of home ownership and professional employment.

Name: Lewes
Description: A South Downs seat centred on the historic town of Lewes, known for its bonfire night celebrations, alongside the working-class ferry port of Newhaven and the ageing resort of Seaford. Surrounding villages are notably wealthy.

Name: Lewisham East
Description: A young and ethnically diverse constituency on the edge of Inner London. Although officially classified as an inner London seat, it has a more suburban character than many neighbouring constituencies and is home to a large Black community alongside growing Asian and mixed-ethnicity populations. Housing is predominantly Victorian terraces, council estates and newer apartment developments, with high levels of both private and social renting. Regeneration around Lewisham town centre continues to attract younger professionals.

Name: Lewisham North
Description: Centred on Deptford and New Cross, this is a densely populated inner London constituency with a large Black population and high levels of social and private renting. Goldsmiths, University of London contributes to a sizeable student and creative population, while Deptford has become one of London's fastest-gentrifying neighbourhoods. Despite this, the constituency retains a strong working-class character.

Name: Leyton and Wanstead
Description: Combining the Victorian suburbs of Wanstead to the dense neighbourhoods of Leyton, this constituency reflects London's changing east. Leyton has become increasingly popular with young professionals priced out of Hackney, while Wanstead retains a more affluent suburban character. The constituency is highly diverse, with a rapidly growing private-rented sector.

Name: Manchester Rusholme
Description: A young, densely populated inner-city seat taking in Rusholme's 'Curry Mile', Fallowfield's student housing, Moss Side and Hulme. One of the most ethnically diverse seats in the country, with large Pakistani and Black communities and very high private renting.

Name: Manchester Withington
Description: A leafy, youthful south Manchester seat covering Chorlton-cum-Hardy, Didsbury and Withington, popular with university and NHS professionals. One of the most highly qualified seats in the country, with a reputation for craft beer bars and an alternative, liberal character.

Name: Mid Sussex
Description: A prosperous West Sussex seat centred on the commuter towns of Burgess Hill and Haywards Heath, with the Prime Meridian running through it. Highly professional and owner-occupied, with picturesque villages such as Cuckfield and Lindfield.

Name: Milton Keynes Central
Description: The core of the planned new town of Milton Keynes, known for its grid-like roads and roundabouts and home to the Open University's headquarters. It has a young, ethnically diverse population and a wide mix of housing types.

Name: North Cotswolds
Description: An affluent, largely rural constituency of Cotswold villages and stone-built market towns such as Moreton-in-Marsh, plus the town-like villages of Brockworth and Churchdown between Gloucester and Cheltenham. Notably older and wealthier than the national average.

Name: North East Hampshire
Description: An affluent, leafy Hampshire seat around Fleet and Hook, with the Roman ruins of Silchester nearby. It has one of the best-educated and most car-owning populations in the country, and one of the lowest rates of deprivation.

Name: North West Essex
Description: A largely rural and affluent constituency centred on the historic market towns of Saffron Walden and Great Dunmow. Strong links to Cambridge, London and Stansted support a highly educated, professional and commuter population.

Name: Norwich South
Description: A diverse and youthful inner-city constituency covering southern Norwich. It has a large student and private-renter population, significant council housing, with the universities, public sector and service industries giving it a more urban and progressive character.

Name: Oxford East
Description: The eastern half of Oxford, taking in the university's historic core as well as the former Cowley car works and the large Blackbird Leys housing estate. It is ethnically diverse and has a large student population alongside significant social housing.

Name: Peckham
Description: One of Britain's most ethnically diverse urban constituencies, centred on Peckham, Camberwell and Nunhead. Historically a working-class area, it has one of the country's largest Black populations and the highest rates of social housing. Recent years have also seen significant gentrification, particularly around Peckham Rye and Bellenden Road, creating an increasingly mixed social profile.

Name: Reading Central
Description: The core of Reading, a large Berkshire town with a long-established university and a modern economy built on digital and technology firms. It has a substantial private-rented and student population, more diverse and urban than the town's outer suburbs.

Name: Reading West and Mid Berkshire
Description: Combining Reading's western suburbs with rural West Berkshire villages such as Pangbourne and Bradfield. It includes the Atomic Weapons Establishment at Aldermaston, and mixes affluent riverside areas with more ordinary suburban estates.

Name: Romford
Description: A suburban constituency centred on the historic market town of Romford, with a strong commuter-belt identity and cultural links to neighbouring Essex. It has historically been one of London's more socially conservative and Brexit-supporting constituencies, although parts of the south of the seat have experienced increasing demographic change.

Name: Romsey and Southampton North
Description: Combining the historic market town of Romsey, with the Palmerston and Mountbatten family seat at Broadlands, and affluent northern suburbs of Southampton. It has a prosperous, professional character and rural Test Valley villages further out.

Name: Rutland and Stamford
Description: A rural and affluent constituency centred on the historic market towns of Stamford, Oakham and Uppingham. It combines attractive countryside, prosperous villages and a strong heritage and tourism economy, while agriculture remains important. The constituency has a notably settled and older population, with high home ownership and a relatively large veteran community, reflecting the presence of military establishments in and around Rutland.

Name: Sheffield Hallam
Description: Sheffield's affluent western suburbs, from Ecclesall and Dore to the university areas of Broomhill and Endcliffe. One of the country's wealthiest and most highly educated seats, with very little social housing.

Name: Slough
Description: A diverse, working-class Berkshire town close to London, with a large South Asian population and significant Muslim and Sikh communities. Its industrial trading estate, once home to the Mars chocolate factory, has long given it a functional, unglamorous character.

Name: South Cotswolds
Description: A wealthy, rural seat straddling the Gloucestershire-Wiltshire border, centred on the historic market town of Cirencester, a former Roman settlement, along with Tetbury and Malmesbury. A popular commuter and second-home area for Swindon, Bath and Bristol.

Name: St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire
Description: A fast-growing Cambridgeshire seat combining St Neots, one of England's fastest-expanding towns, with the purpose-built village of Cambourne and villages closer to Cambridge. New housing has brought a younger, more mobile population, though qualifications and professional employment run higher in the Cambridge-facing villages than in St Neots itself.

Name: Stratford-on-Avon
Description: An affluent, rural Warwickshire seat beneath the Cotswolds, centred on Shakespeare's birthplace and taking in the Forest of Arden and small market towns. It has high rates of home ownership and professional employment, and a notably elderly population.

Name: Surrey Heath
Description: An affluent, heavily wooded Surrey seat centred on Camberley and Frimley, home to the Sandhurst military academy and a strong army presence. Highly owner-occupied with very high car ownership, it has a settled, suburban commuter character.

Name: Sussex Weald
Description: A rural East Sussex seat with no large towns, taking in Crowborough, Hailsham and the northern edge of Ashdown Forest, the setting for A.A. Milne's Winnie the Pooh stories. Affluent and heavily owner-occupied, with a notably elderly population.

Name: Sutton Coldfield
Description: An affluent, leafy Birmingham suburb built around its own historic park, retaining a distinct identity from the surrounding city. It has very high rates of home ownership and professional employment, with a growing Hindu and Sikh community.

Name: Swindon North
Description: The more suburban and rural half of Swindon, extending north through Haydon Wick to the small town of Highworth and villages towards the Gloucestershire border. Historically linked to the Pressed Steel and BMW car works, it is more owner-occupied than Swindon South.

Name: Swindon South
Description: Covers Swindon's urban core and town centre, historically shaped by the Great Western Railway works and now home to Nationwide's headquarters. More ethnically diverse than the north of the town, with a notable Goan community.

Name: Tonbridge
Description: A wooded, rural Kent seat along the Medway valley, with hop gardens, orchards and oast houses giving it a classic 'Garden of England' character. It also takes in grand estates such as Hever Castle and Penshurst Place, and has a well-off, well-educated population.

Name: Tunbridge Wells
Description: A fashionable former Georgian spa town, whose association with prim conservatism gave rise to the phrase 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells'. Its well-regarded grammar schools draw an affluent, professional commuter population.

Name: Uxbridge and South Ruislip
Description: A suburban outer west London seat, this constituency has a varied social profile. Uxbridge serves as a major commercial and retail centre for west London, while South Ruislip has a quieter residential character with high owner occupation. Brunel University contributes a sizeable student population and international community.

Name: Warwick and Leamington
Description: Combining the historic town of Warwick, with its Norman castle, and the Regency spa town of Royal Leamington Spa. It's an affluent, well-qualified seat with a notable Sikh community concentrated in south Leamington.

Name: Watford
Description: A diverse London-commuter town anchored by a major regional shopping centre and Watford FC. The constituency has one of Hertfordshire's largest South Asian communities, with substantial Hindu, Muslim and Pakistani populations, and a notably younger and more ethnically mixed profile than the rest of the county.

Name: Welwyn Hatfield
Description: Combining the planned garden city of Welwyn Garden City with the university town of Hatfield, this seat blends a large student population with more traditional New Town communities. Hatfield's aerospace past (once home to de Havilland) has given way to the university and business parks, and the seat now has one of the country's largest Chinese populations.

Name: West Aberdeenshire and Kincardine
Description: A prosperous, rural Aberdeenshire seat following Royal Deeside - including Balmoral Castle - through picturesque towns like Aboyne and Ballater, plus the coastal resort of Stonehaven and farming country toward Angus. An affluent, elderly and highly owner-occupied seat, among the least deprived in Scotland.

Name: West Ham and Beckton
Description: Centred on the Royal Docks and Beckton, this constituency has been transformed by large-scale regeneration and housing development. It is one of Britain's most ethnically diverse constituencies, with a large number of Black and Asian residents, very high levels of social and private renting and a notably young population. Around a quarter of residents are Muslim.

Name: West Suffolk
Description: A rural West Suffolk constituency centred on Newmarket, the historic capital of British horseracing, together with the manufacturing town of Haverhill and the US airbases at Mildenhall and Lakenheath. American service personnel give the area a notably large White Other population, alongside racing- and forestry-related employment.

Name: Winchester
Description: A wealthy, historic cathedral city, extending into the pretty Meon Valley villages and small towns to the east. Highly educated and professional, it also has a significant student population from the University of Winchester.

Name: Witney
Description: A west Oxfordshire market town built on historic wool wealth, extending into the Cotswolds and taking in the RAF base at Brize Norton. Affluent and largely rural, with picturesque towns such as Burford and Lechlade.

Name: Wycombe
Description: Centred on High Wycombe, once a centre of the furniture-making industry, with wooded Chiltern villages such as Turville, used as a filming location for The Vicar of Dibley, beyond. It has a significant and long-established Pakistani community alongside more rural, traditional areas.

Name: Ashford
Description: A Kent railway town at a busy rail junction, extending east towards the Channel Tunnel, with a mix of new private housing estates and more traditional working-class neighbourhoods. Surrounding villages add a more rural character.

Name: Barking
Description: A working-class East London constituency centred on the historic town of Barking. Once one of London's whitest areas, it has undergone rapid demographic change and is now one of the capital's most ethnically diverse constituencies. Extensive regeneration, high levels of social housing and a relatively young population continue to reshape the area.

Name: Basildon and Billericay
Description: Basildon has a strong working-class and industrial heritage, while Billericay is more middle-class and commuter-oriented. Manufacturing, logistics, retail and commuting into London all play an important role in the local economy.

Name: Bexhill and Battle
Description: A coastal East Sussex seat between Hastings and Eastbourne, taking in the historic site of the Battle of Hastings at Battle Abbey and Rudyard Kipling's former home at Bateman's. It has one of the highest proportions of pensioners in the country.

Name: Bexleyheath and Crayford
Description: A predominantly suburban outer London constituency characterised by lower middle-class neighbourhoods, high levels of owner occupation and relatively low levels of both private and social renting. Compared with most of London, it has an older and less ethnically diverse population.

Name: Bournemouth East
Description: The more prosperous half of Bournemouth's seafront, including the wealthy suburb of Queen's Park alongside more deprived areas such as Boscombe. Tourism and banking, including a large JP Morgan office, are the main employers.

Name: Bournemouth West
Description: The more diverse half of the seaside town of Bournemouth, with a large student population drawn by its university. Tourism and banking are the main employers, alongside pockets of deprivation around West Howe.

Name: Broxbourne
Description: Suburban constituency that combines North  London commuter characteristics with a high propotion of self employed tradespeople. The South of the constituency around Cheshunt shares many characteristics with North London, including a large White - Other population of mostly Greek Cypriots. The North of the constituency around Hoddesdon has a more provincial characteristic

Name: Bury South
Description: Takes in Whitefield, Prestwich and part of Radcliffe, a gentrifying commuter belt for Manchester professionals priced out of Chorlton and Didsbury. It has one of the highest Jewish populations in Britain, with a significant strictly Orthodox community around Kersal and Broughton Park.

Name: Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket
Description: Combines the affluent cathedral town of Bury St Edmunds with the Ipswich commuter town of Stowmarket, and rural villages in between. Light Industry and Food Production are central to the area

Name: Canterbury
Description: The historic cathedral city of Canterbury, whose large student population, drawn by two universities, gives it a younger profile than most of Kent. It also takes in the coastal towns of Whitstable and Tankerton to the north.

Name: Central Devon
Description: A sprawling, rural mid-Devon seat with no single centre, linking the wool towns of Crediton and Ashburton with the Dartmoor market town of Okehampton. Small businesses and commuting to Exeter and Plymouth dominate the economy.

Name: Central Suffolk and North Ipswich
Description: A rural seat comprising affluent Suffolk towns of Framlingham and Needham Market with the mostly middle class Ipswich suburbs of Castle Hill and Kesgrave.

Name: Chelmsford
Description: A prosperous Commuter town, Chelmsford is an employment centre in its own right, with significant financial, public-sector and technology employment, whilst rail links support London commuters.

Name: Chester North and Neston
Description: Combines the historic Roman city centre of Chester, now popular with students and young professionals, with the separate town of Neston on the Dee estuary, linked by a thin rural strip. Younger and more highly qualified than its southern neighbour.

Name: Colchester
Description: Colchester combines a substantial student population associated with the University of Essex with a significant military presence, a growing professional population and extensive new housing development. The city has a large public sector workforce, and a younger and more diverse population that much of Essex

Name: Coventry East
Description: A working-class seat covering Coventry's northern and eastern suburbs, including Foleshill and Wyken, with a large South Asian population including significant Muslim and Sikh communities. Graduate rates are below average.

Name: Croydon West
Description: A diverse urban constituency centred on Croydon town centre and its western suburbs. It has a young population, one of the UK's largest Black communities, a significant Asian community, extensive regeneration and relatively high levels of private renting. Once a major commercial centre for south London, Croydon continues to evolve through large-scale redevelopment.

Name: Dartford
Description: A fast-growing Kent town on the edge of Greater London, near the Dartford Crossing, Bluewater shopping centre and Ebbsfleet International station. Increasingly popular with London commuters, it has become notably more ethnically diverse in recent years.

Name: Daventry
Description: A largely rural constituency of market towns, villages and expanding commuter settlements. Agriculture, logistics and warehousing play major economic roles, reflecting its central location and excellent motorway connections.

Name: Derby North
Description: A suburban  constituency covering northern Derby. It combines established suburban neighbourhoods with more deprived inner-city areas and has a significant manufacturing base centred around engineering and aerospace. The university of Derby and many of its students live here

Name: Derby South
Description: Covering Derby city centre and southern suburbs, this constituency is ethnically diverse and economically varied. It includes large student and minority ethnic populations, around a quarter of which are asian and a fifth Muslim, alongside major employers such as Rolls-Royce and Toyota nearby.

Name: Droitwich and Evesham
Description: Combining the spa town of Droitwich, built on ancient salt deposits, with the market town of Evesham amid the fruit-growing Vale of Evesham. It has a notably elderly population and a strong agricultural economy.

Name: Eastbourne
Description: A genteel Victorian seaside resort on the Sussex coast, built up by the Dukes of Devonshire, with a notably elderly population, especially in the affluent Meads area. It retains an old-fashioned resort character with theatres and seafront gardens.

Name: Exeter
Description: Devon's university city and administrative hub, home to the Met Office and a large student population. Combines a historic centre - much rebuilt after WWII bombing - with modern suburbs and the riverside town of Topsham.

Name: Exmouth and Exeter East
Description: Combines the seaside town of Exmouth, more working-class and youthful than its neighbours, with the genteel resort of Budleigh Salterton and Exeter's eastern suburbs including Topsham. An ageing, largely affluent seat just outside Exeter.

Name: Fareham and Waterlooville
Description: A largely suburban Hampshire seat combining Fareham and Portchester with Waterlooville and Cowplain to the north. Mostly owner-occupied and modestly middle-class, with little in the way of striking wealth or deprivation.

Name: Faversham and Mid Kent
Description: An overwhelmingly rural Kent seat with no large town, centred on the historic market town of Faversham, home to Britain's oldest brewer, Shepherd Neame. Orchards and market gardening dominate the surrounding countryside, and the population is notably elderly.

Name: Filton and Bradley Stoke
Description: A South Gloucestershire seat on Bristol's northern fringe, mixing the new commuter town of Bradley Stoke with older, working-class Filton and Patchway, long associated with aerospace engineering at BAE and Rolls-Royce. A large defence and MoD presence remains nearby.

Name: Folkestone and Hythe
Description: A Kent coastal seat centred on Folkestone and Hythe, home to the Channel Tunnel terminal, with the flat, sparsely populated Romney Marsh, sometimes called 'the fifth continent' for its isolated character, to the south. Qualifications are below average and private renting is notably high.

Name: Frome and East Somerset
Description: A north-east Somerset seat centred on Frome, a historic wool town with a growing arts and alternative scene, taking in the former Somerset coalfield around Midsomer Norton and Radstock. More affluent and professional than the coalfield's industrial past suggests.

Name: Fylde
Description: An affluent, settled seaside seat on the Lancashire coast around Lytham St Annes, with a notably elderly population and one of the highest owner-occupation rates in the region. BAE Systems' Warton aerospace site and Royal Lytham's Open Championship golf course are major local features.

Name: Glasgow West
Description: Stretches from the affluent West End through middle-class suburbs to the large post-war housing estate of Drumchapel. Shipbuilding heritage survives at a naval yard in Scotstoun, alongside a growing student population near the university.

Name: Glastonbury and Somerton
Description: A rural Somerset seat taking in the shoe-making town of Street, the mystical hilltop town of Glastonbury and the increasingly fashionable, wealthy town of Bruton. Notably elderly, affluent and overwhelmingly white.

Name: Hamble Valley
Description: A suburban seat along the River Hamble between Southampton and Fareham, centred on the growing town of Hedge End and the villages of Botley and Hamble-le-Rice, known for sailing. It has a comfortably off, owner-occupying population without being especially wealthy.

Name: Harrogate and Knaresborough
Description: A genteel former spa town, still a conference and tourism hub, paired with the smaller, historic market town of Knaresborough on the River Nidd. An affluent, highly educated seat more akin to the southern Home Counties than the rest of Yorkshire.

Name: Hastings and Rye
Description: A Sussex coastal seat combining the faded Victorian resort of Hastings, with its historic fishing fleet on the Stade beach, and the medieval Cinque Port town of Rye. It has a mix of working-class seaside areas and more affluent rural villages.

Name: Hemel Hempstead
Description: A post war town containing Planned residential neighbourhoods, major industrial, logistics and public sector areas, and a London commuter character. The constituency has a diverse and relatively young population, with substantial private and social rented housing alongside more established suburban communities

Name: Herne Bay and Sandwich
Description: A Kent coastal seat combining the seaside resort of Herne Bay with the historic Cinque Port of Sandwich, whose harbour silted up centuries ago. It has an elderly, largely white population and a tourism-dependent economy.

Name: Honiton and Sidmouth
Description: An affluent, rural east Devon seat combining the lace-making town of Honiton with the genteel coastal resort of Sidmouth and smaller towns including Axminster and Seaton. Notably elderly, with dramatic red cliffs along its coastline.

Name: Huntingdon
Description: A mixed market town an rural constituency centered on Huntingdon, St Ives and surrounding villages. It has experienced substantial population growth through new housing and commuter development, supported by strong road and rail connections. The constituency combines agriculture and rural communities with professional employment, logistics and a growing commuter population.

Name: Isle of Wight East
Description: The eastern half of the Isle of Wight, taking in Ryde and the seaside resorts of Sandown and Shanklin. Tourism-dependent and served by ferries and a small railway, it has one of the oldest populations of any English seat.

Name: Isle of Wight West
Description: The western half of the Isle of Wight, combining the county town of Newport and the yachting centre of Cowes with the more remote, rural villages of West Wight around Freshwater. It has an elderly population and a strong sailing and tourism tradition.

Name: Leicester South
Description: A diverse inner-city constituency covering Leicester city centre, the University of Leicester and De Montfort University. It has large South Asian, Muslim and student populations, with the economy centred on education, retail and professional services.

Name: Luton South and South Bedfordshire
Description: A highly diverse constituency combining southern Luton with more suburban and rural parts of Bedfordshire. Luton has large Pakistani and Bangladeshi communities and a strong Muslim presence, while the south Bedfordshire villages are whiter and more affluent

Name: Macclesfield
Description: A former silk-manufacturing town in Cheshire, now a Manchester commuter base, with affluent surrounding villages including Prestbury, known for its footballer residents. An ageing, well-qualified and largely white, home-owning population.

Name: Maidstone and Malling
Description: Kent's county town, Maidstone, on the River Medway, alongside the suburban Mallings and Aylesford. Once known for brewing, toffee-making and paper manufacturing, it now has a more commuter-oriented economy and a notable Gurkha community.

Name: Melksham and Devizes
Description: Combines the market towns of Melksham, Devizes and Bradford-on-Avon in Wiltshire. Melksham retains a manufacturing base including tyre and rail-brake factories, while Bradford-on-Avon's historic wool industry has given way to tourism.

Name: Melton and Syston
Description: A constituency combining the affluent commuter town of Syston, the Leicester suburb of Thurmaston, andthe rural market town of Melton Mowbray, famous for its pork pies and Stilton cheese. Agriculture, food production and commuting to Leicester are key features.

Name: Meriden and Solihull East
Description: A sharply divided seat combining affluent commuter villages such as Meriden and Dorridge with the large, deprived Chelmsley Wood council estate. Home ownership and professional employment are high outside the estate.

Name: Mid Bedfordshire
Description: Affluent Rural constituency containing market towns, villages and expanding commuter settlements such as Flitwick and Ampthill. Home ownership and professional occupations are high. Located between Milton Keyenes, Luton and Bedford, the constituency has a stongly commuter characteristic

Name: Mid Leicestershire
Description: A largely suburban and rural constituency surrounding the northern and western edges of Leicester. Characterised by affluent villages, expanding commuter housing and high levels of owner occupation, and a sizeable Hindi population in the suburb of Birstall

Name: Mitcham and Morden
Description: A densely populated and ethnically diverse constituency in eastern Merton. It has a higher proportion of flats, social housing and lower-income households than many outer London suburban seats, although it also contains more suburban areas around Morden.

Name: New Forest East
Description: Combining the Waterside towns of Totton and Hythe, dominated by the giant Fawley oil refinery, with the quieter New Forest villages of Beaulieu and Brockenhurst. Affluent and heavily owner-occupied, with a notably elderly population.

Name: New Forest West
Description: Covering much of the New Forest itself, with its heathland, wild ponies and Crown land, alongside the coastal towns of New Milton and Lymington. It has an exceptionally elderly population and functions largely as a retirement and tourism area.

Name: North Bedfordshire
Description: A largely rural constituency surrounding Bedford and containing market towns, villages and growing commuter communities. It combines traditional agricultural areas with newer housing development and an increasingly affluent, professional population.

Name: North Dorset
Description: A rural seat of market towns - Blandford Forum, Shaftesbury and Gillingham - amid the Blackmore Vale and Cranborne Chase. Notably elderly and agricultural, with a large army camp at Blandford.

Name: North East Fife
Description: The East Neuk fishing villages and the university town of St Andrews, home to Scotland's oldest university and the birthplace of golf. An affluent, highly educated seat with a large student population.

Name: North East Hertfordshire
Description: A largely affluent constituency combining Letchworth Garden City with the market towns of Royston and Buntingford. It has a strong professional and commuter character, with technology and science employment particularly important around Royston.

Name: North East Somerset and Hanham
Description: Spanning the suburban fringe between Bristol and Bath, taking in the commuter town of Keynsham and former coalfield villages such as Timsbury and Paulton. A prosperous, largely white-collar seat with high owner-occupation.

Name: North Somerset
Description: A commuter belt southwest of Bristol taking in Portishead, Clevedon and Nailsea, with Bristol Airport and Portbury Docks nearby. An affluent, highly owner-occupied seat with an elderly population.

Name: North West Cambridgeshire
Description: A mixed urban and rural constituency centred on Peterborough's expanding souther suburbs. New housing development, logistics and manufacturing give it a younger and more diverse character than much of rural Cambridgeshire.

Name: North West Hampshire
Description: A rural north Hampshire seat centred on Andover, a post-war expansion town, with Highclere Castle, the filming location for Downton Abbey, nearby. Overwhelmingly white with above-average social housing.

Name: Nottingham South
Description: A socially mixed constituency stretching from Nottingham city centre through student-heavy areas such as Lenton and Dunkirk towards more settled suburbs including Clifton. There is a high propotion of students and private renting due to both the University of Nottingham and Nottingham Trent being located in the seat,while the constituency is also ethnically diverse with sizeable South Asian and Black communities

Name: Peterborough
